best_for: Photographers and archivists with folders full of mixed image formats who want one fast viewer that also renames, converts and tags in batches.

points.title: Free at home, paid at work
points.text: It is free for private and educational use, including non-profits. Company use needs a license, listed at 29 euros for one seat and dropping with volume, down to 3.90 euros each past 1,000. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Opens almost anything
points.text: The publisher lists support for more than 500 image formats and export to about 70. Old scans and odd formats you inherited can usually be viewed and converted without another app.

points.title: Batch jobs built in
points.text: Batch convert, batch rename and timestamp changes come in the box, using the same engine as XnConvert. It also has a duplicate file finder, lossless JPEG rotation, contact sheets and slideshows.

points.title: Metadata you can edit
points.text: It reads EXIF and edits IPTC and XMP fields, so captions, keywords and credits can be written into the files themselves rather than kept in a separate catalog.

points.title: No ads in the free version
points.text: The download page states there is no adware or spyware. Donations are optional; nothing is held back from private users.

points.title: Installer or portable on Windows
points.text: Windows gets a machine-wide x64 installer and a zip you can run without installing. The Windows listing keeps 28 versions; macOS (a universal build for macOS 12 and later) and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux is x64 only
points.text: The Flathub build is marked verified for the developer and runs on x64 only. There is no Arm64 Linux package listed here.
